#3672. Marvelous, developer of the Story of Seasons series, opens up voluntary redundancy scheme as it seeks to reduce headcount by 65 employees

The offer is described as an "early retirement" program.

Marvelous, the studio known for its work on the Story of Seasons series as well as the upcoming Eternal Anima, has announced the introduction of a voluntary redundancy scheme. Through this program, it's aiming to lower its headcount by 65 employees.

Per Automaton, this "early retirement" program is part of an effort to restructure its console business, which refers to non-mobile, non-live-service games under its umbrella.

The reason for this change is the shifting environment in game development, namely the growing scope of development and elongated development cycles. The company cites a need to optimise its workforce and shift towards flexibility, per the introduction of the early retirement program.

Marvelous will begin gathering applications, with those choosing to take the company up on the offer set to leave at the end of the financial year in March 2027. These employees will receive a bonus as part of their redundancy package, as well as assistance finding new employment elsewhere if they desire it.

Marvelous emphasised that despite this program, it still sees console game development as one of its core businesses. This comes in the same financial year Marvelous reported a 1,105 percent increase in profit between April 2026 - September 2026, credited to overseas sales of both new indie releases and older console games.

#3671. Team Ninja Is Using AI For Quality Assurance, But Insists Creative Choices ‘Must Be Done By Humans’

Team Ninja is known, in part, for developing difficult games, but producers Kohei Shibata and Masakazu Hirayama emphasized during an interview with INVEN Global at GCON 2026 in South Korea that thereâs a key difference between difficult and unfair. The pair also spoke about how the Koei Tecmo subsidiary approaches the use of AI in games development, and an awkward compromise between implementing the technology for repetitive QA tasks, while arguing that “what matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands.”

Shibata and Hirayama are best known for their work as producers on the Nioh and Wo Long series respectively, two games that take the combat-driven difficulty of the iconic Ninja Gaiden franchise and transpose it onto the world of samurai and Chinese mythology. Before the topic of AI arose, the two discussed the crucial role of player interaction and movement in their games, beginning with the similarities between all three franchises and most notably their swordplay and the focus on timing your attacks and reading an opponentâs next move. According to both, this process of requiring a player to learn an enemyâs next move and counter is key to straddling the line between challenging and frustrating play.

âI consider Nioh to be samurai action,â explained Shibata. âSamurai combat involves stillness and movement. You stand firmly grounded, observing the opponent’s moves, and deliver a sharp strike the instant an opening appears.â Meanwhile, for Hirayama on Wo Long, that game was defined by âaggressive Chinese martial arts action,â where âattack and defense flow together seamlesslyâ and where âaggressively attacking is important, but defense must also lead directly into the next attack.â

The two go on to argue that it’s important to make a game that is polished in a way that reduces friction between a player’s action and consequence. If a person fails, it must be their fault, not the game’s. âI believe [the core essence of action games is] control responsiveness,â Shibata explained. âWhen a player presses a button, the character must move exactly as they intended. If you press a button and the character doesn’t react properly, it causes frustration. Conversely, if a slight input causes an exaggerated movement, it feels awkward. Therefore, responsiveness to input must be simple and intuitive, and the movement must be communicated rapidly.â

We have seen numerous studios speak out in recent times about where they will and wonât use AI. While some Japanese developers are embracing the technology, others are more cautious, either avoiding it entirely or insisting they only use the technology for optimizing their development framework while leaving creative choices to humans. The latter is the direction being taken by Capcom with its next generation of RE Engine, and appears to also be the choice being made by Team Ninja, who are already using AI for QA purposes.

As Shibata explained, âCurrently, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows. If we can use AI to shorten task times, we can dedicate that saved time toward elevating the game’s overall quality. In that sense, using AI is beneficial. However, since it is still a new technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions.” He continued,

What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future.

Where, if anywhere, is an acceptable use of AI is a topic that remains up for debate, but it appears many developers are settling into a space where it is used to handle repetitive tasks. The use of AI in QA actually predates the modern conversations of generative AI, and doesnât necessarily rely on the tech: Sony, for instance, has been experimenting with AI for many years to test games. Whether this is something audiences are willing to tolerate, or indeed is something that will further threaten jobs in the games industry, remains to be seen.

#3670. Rockstar boss "so grateful" to have kept GTA 6's big prologue twist a secret - and reveals Tomás' story could have been very different

"Multiple times throughout development, people were like, 'Can it not be...'"

If you've played the first 20 minutes or so of Grand Theft Auto 6, you'll know there's a hugely significant plot revelation there - one Rockstar somehow managed to keep entirely secret until the game's launch.

It's somewhat miraculous they did, given the many leaks the studio has suffered until now. And while, frankly, the embargo restrictions around discussing it in our GTA 6 review made a deeper analysis of Jason and Lucia's story more than a little awkward, I'm also mostly glad it remained a surprise. It's one of the great twists delivered in a game of this kind.

Speaking to Eurogamer in an interview shortly before GTA 6 was released, Rockstar Games' head of development Rob Nelson discussed the secret and, notably, the fact the team also discussed going another way entirely.

Spoilers for GTA 6's opening half hour - and further backstory around that moment from later in the game - below.

The big twist of course is that Jason and Lucia have a young child, Tomás, who we see Lucia abandoning in order to rob a store at gunpoint during the game's prologue.

It's an astonishing moment, both in the complexity it immediately lends Lucia, who is at once painted in a more negative light as a result, and in the stakes it affords her and Jason. This is the first time GTA's protagonists have genuine, human stakes that underpin their actions during the game's story, and at the same time Rockstar, in doing so, opens a route for itself to offering a far more nuanced take on modern crime.

But it was also something of a risk – and a hotly debated one, as Nelson told me during our conversation – as giving the game's protagonists that kind of narrative weight ran somewhat counter to the crime movie, straight-to-the-action thrills of previous GTAs.

"I'm so grateful that we managed to keep that under wraps," Nelson said. The subversion of expectations was intentional. "You feel like you maybe know these characters, or what the game or the story is going to be about, and then in the first 10, 15 minutes, it takes on a completely different context."It was an idea that came about organically. "But the idea of the character wanting something that maybe is at odds with what you thought you wanted as a player coming in, which is amassing as much material wealth as possible, and as many cars, and as many things," he said, was something Rockstar found particularly compelling.

The next point of the studio's focus then became the justification for Lucia's decision, Nelson explained. "The story was always, broadly, going to go through some of the major beats that it did," once Rockstar decided on the key points of the protagonists being a couple and them having a child. "But the details of the relationship, the narrative details of it, we dialled in a lot - because we're doing a lot there. She's leaving a kid early on – that's not a very sympathetic move to make."

That led to the decision to show, later in the story, more about why Lucia opted to leave Tomás in that moment. "Many chapters later, where [Jason] is like: 'What? Why did you do that?' And she has a flashback to sort of being at her wit's end," Nelson said, which then flows into the question of why she left Jason in the first place. "Cal asks Jason, 'Why did she leave?' And so, well, she didn't know she was pregnant at the time. 'Okay, but why didn't she call you?' 'Well, because I might've told her I didn't want [to be a father].' So you have to just make sure that you can understand both of their perspectives."

The tension from the fact they had a child, and that the two of them were away from their son as you play the game, was significant enough to become a point of discussion within the studio.

"Multiple times throughout development, we had this child, and people are like, 'Can it not be, like, theirs?'" Nelson said. "'Could it be like her little sister? Could it be– because I really feel bad having a good time in Vice City…' and the questions are valid," he continued. "But it wouldn't be powerful if not. So it was up to us to figure out how [you resolve that tension]."

Like with Lucia's justification for leaving Tomás - revealed in a striking dream-slash-flashback later in the game, that mixes typically exaggerated Rockstar satire with genuine social commentary - this then led to a cascade of other character moments. "How about he's in a better position than he would ever be with them, and so he's with her aunt, who's way more stable, and has a loving husband and other little kids, and he's always having a good time?" Nelson said.

He points to a conversation between Jason and Lucia in the game's first chapter as another example. "Very early on, in chapter one, they have this chat where he's like, 'Let's FaceTime - FruitFace is the thing we use - and she's like, 'No, I don't want to confuse him. He's better off until we get our shit together.' And he's like 'Okay' and she's like, 'It's not a cop-out', and he's like, 'No, no, I met my father on the other side of a glass divider, so I'm kind of trying to break that cycle.' And that's right in chapter one, and so it's a thread all the way through."

The result, then, is that the decision to add Tomás ultimately shaped many of the key parts of Jason and Lucia's characters, from their relationships with their own parents – Jason's being in jail, and Lucia's mother too narcissistic to help – to what is, really, the entire narrative arc of the story. And rightly so; a child is a big deal, and one of many reasons why GTA 6 is able to tap into something deeper than any of the previous games in the series before.

We've much more from our interview with Rob Nelson to come over the following days. In the meantime, he discussed why Rockstar made a form of honour system a core part of GTA 6's design (spoiler: because thinking more deeply about your in-game choices is fun). And in other Rockstar news, the studio has surprised those keeping up with its ongoing unionisation efforts by voting against formal recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers' Union.

If you replayed The Witcher 3 in its shiny new remastered form and got absolutely bodied by a couple of werewolf fights you thought were easier back when you had more youthful reflexes, don't worry—the problem wasn't your aging brain and hands after all. It was a bug that's been caught and exterminated in patch 5.02. "Fixed an issue where werewolves could regenerate health too quickly on higher difficulty settings," the patch notes say, "making them impossible to defeat."

Another problem some players had with The Witcher 3 Remastered was its lighting, with interiors in particular looking too dark while some other locations were washed-out flashbangs. Good news: "Fixed various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes," the patch notes say, "including overly bright or dark areas, inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering." They've also "Fixed various lighting issues with hair when Path Tracing is enabled" and "Made various Path Tracing and Ray Reconstruction optimizations and visual improvements, including lighting, shadows, and water rendering."

That's all positive stuff, but the balance changes to various signs and mutations will be more controversial. The Remastered version launched with buffs to Witcher signs that made them useful even if you didn't specialize in them, but it may have overdone things a little. This patch walks back some of the potential for you to dominate the entire game with an Aard build, though changes like reducing the Catalyst skill's bonus to Aard and Igni intensity by 10% don't seem like they'll totally change the way you play.

I get that people don't like skill nerfs in singleplayer games, but I can also see CD Projekt anticipating next year's Songs of the Past DLC. They don't want to hear a bunch of players say, "It sucked because I trivialized the whole thing with a broken build I got by copying a YouTuber." If some skill nerfs and a reduction to stamina regeneration in combat mean you have to drink more potions to get your signs off, it probably won't ruin your fun.

Oh, and if you couldn't complete your Gwent collection because Zoltan Chivay's card didn't show up, the patch notes say it'll now appear in the correct place under the Hanged Man's Tree in Velen. Time to go back and get that 100% achievement at last.

However, it might have have found a new medium through which to claw back its cash: the movies. Amidst Saudi Arabiaâs many other investments is new film studio The Arena, which has just announced Metal Slug as the latest property from the game studio to be in the works for a movie adaptation.

First reported by Variety, the studio announced that the adaptation of the side-scrolling military action platformer is going ahead, withÂ I Love My Dad director James Morosini attached to the project. An initial plot loosely based on the already thin narrative of theÂ Metal Slug series has also been revealed, centered on a misfit quartet of army recruits known as Marco Rossi, Tarma Roving, Eri Kasamoto and Fio Germi, as they stand up to General Morden to save the world from evil. #3667. Are you a warlock tired of being summon-kicked in World of Warcraft: Forever? There's now a mod to fight back with

Being recruited to a World of Warcraft party as a warlock, only to be swiftly kicked again after using your powers to magically summon the party members together in the same place, may soon become a thing of the past. All thanks to a mod made by one especially peeved warlock.

The practice of exploiting warlocks in this way is called summon-kicking, and aside from the in-game reporting feature, there is little recourse to admonish such behavior.

Enter Summoners Union, the add-on mod, which grants the ability to flag and track players who summon-kick thereby building a collective case against them.

The mod was showcased on the World of Warcraft: Forever Reddit by user 274Moons, highlighting its ability to flag players after they boot you from a party, but also that it warns you if anyone in the party has a record of summon-kicking. It can also be combined with an in-game chat channel where warlock comrades can pull together and discuss and ultimately maybe fend off this nasty behavior.

"I play a lock and got tired of the usual 'hey can you summon?', ten minutes at the stone, last person comes through, *You have been removed from the group.*," 274Moons wrote. "So I made an addon about it. It's called The Summoners Union."

According to the add-on's creator, over 500 Warlocks have already downloaded Summon Union. It's a relatively small number in comparison to the wider World of Warcraft: Forever population, but it's a notable start.

"Thank you for this, I hate being just a taxi," wrote user Gregore997. Others also were quick to thank 274Moons for their service to all the Warlocks out there, such as Nangz who wrote: "Please keep the community sharing!".

World of Warcraft: Forever has been out for a little while now and it's been received rather well, breaking records for the series in terms of active players. The playerbase is currently awaiting the release of the game's first raids next month.

#3664. Hollow Knight: Silksong's first big expansion, Sea of Sorrow, comes out in two weeks - and seems to include a fishing minigame

Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry debuted a special 'Cherry Time Special Presentation' today (27th November), with the aim of bringing more information to light about the game's first big DLC offering, Sea of Sorrows, but also provide a nice little springboard for some other indie titles.

But first, the reason we're all here: Sea of Sorrow is "an expansion like we've never done before", says Team Cherry, before showing off a trailer for the content - which will be free for all players, in case you've forgetten. The trailer confirms the release date for the DLC, 11th December, and teases some new environments, enemies, bosses and - right at the end - what looks like a fishing mini-game. But of course, this is a nautical-themed expansion, after all.

Team Cherry has hinted at the future of Silksong before. Recently, and more than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong finally began arriving on players' doorsteps. These editions seemed to tease previously unconfirmed "free content packs" (note the plural). "The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet read in the physical editions. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!" We have no hint on what will happen next for Silksong, though, off the back of this presentation.

#3663. Why Kate Middleton's Return to William's Side Says a Lot About the Future of the Monarchy

After days of rumors circulating about Kate Middleton’s possible participation in the trip to India, confirmation came only at the last minute. This news came as a surprise in many ways, even though the princess’s presence was expected. Her involvement in this tour of India deserves attention, especially in light of the increasingly important role she plays alongside Prince William, who will be king. The trip to India, significant in its own right, also included an important meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aimed at strengthening relations between the United Kingdom and India. This high-profile diplomatic meeting was added after it was confirmed that Modi would return in time from his trip to the Philippines.

The Prince and Princess of Wales arrive at the Earthshot ceremony

Kate’s participation in the royal tour was made official by Kensington Palace only the day before departure to allow the princess to assess her condition right up until the last minute and determine whether she could handle such a demanding trip, following her recovery. But once she arrived in Mumbai, Catherine proved she was ready to do more than initially planned. The princess appeared, as always, impeccable and smiling—perhaps even more so than usual—in her customary understated and polished style. She greeted the crowd and met with people who had come to see her, participating in events alongside her husband.

From the first day of this three-day tour—which began on the anniversary of their official engagement— Kate immediately displayed her characteristic good-natured spirit, evident in past tours as well, by joining Prince William in a game of gully cricket—a street version of the sport—alongside local children and teenagers. Serving as host was Sachin Tendulkar, an Indian sports legend whom the couple had already met during their previous visit to the country in 2016. The two princes put their skills to the test with little formality. They then took a ride on the Mumbai metro—a scene we’d already seen in London in candid photos when the Princess of Wales traveled on a bus in celebration of London Poppy Day.

The Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony

The highlight was the awards ceremony in Mumbai on the evening of the second day, when the Princess of Wales unexpectedly took the stage to deliver a speech dedicated to the power of nature, health, and healing. Her speech was kept secret until the last moment, so much so that not even the celebrities and other guests in attendance knew the Princess of Wales would be speaking. “Nature is precious,” the princess said. “We are not separate from it. We are part of it, deeply connected in ways both visible and unseen…the health of the planet and our natural world is inseparable from our own, and when it thrives, so do we,” she continued. “I have seen firsthand how nature has the power to heal and enrich our daily lives, but so much remains under threat.” “There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time."

Catherine then presented the award in the “Protect and Restore Nature” category, dedicated to the protection and restoration of ecosystems. “The people we’re celebrating tonight are a huge part of that story. Their work will inspire and create seismic change that will improve lives for generations to come,” she said.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony

Over the past three days, William and Kate have been busy meeting about sustainability, innovation, transportation, culture, and relations between the two countries. William is, in fact, assuming an increasingly prominent role on the international stage, supporting the United Kingdom’s diplomatic relations through his travels, which Middleton’s presence reinforced. This time, however, it was not simply a princess accompanying her husband on an official visit, but a woman who, after her illness and a long hiatus from major trips abroad, chose to return to her rightful role—and one the public has long expected her to fill.

The Prince and Princess of Wales with some Earthshot Prize winners

It’s worth noting that this is the first time in four years—since her illness—that Kate has accompanied Prince William on an official overseas mission. The last such occasion was in December 2022, when the couple traveled to Boston, Massachusetts, for the Earthshot Prize ceremony. Her participation in the trip to India thus reflects her desire to gradually resume her international role, as well as her awareness of just how important her presence is to the monarchy.

After her cancer diagnosis in 2024, Catherine prioritized her health and family, returning to public engagements without rushing things. However, her trip to Reggio Emilia, Italy, last May marked an important first step. On that occasion, she appeared visibly engaged and enthusiastic, and in subsequent statements, she hinted at her desire to travel more and gradually resume international engagements. “So I’m so glad it went well for her. I think she came back buzzing.” William said, describing his wife’s mood after that trip. Court circles had also hinted that Catherine wished to gradually resume a more active schedule.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony

Her return to work, however, was approached gradually, respecting the time needed for her recovery. It’s a journey that Kate herself described with great sincerity in a recent interview published last week in Country Life, a magazine for which Prince William served as guest editor. “I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear. There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time,” the princess said, emphasizing that recovery does not necessarily proceed in a steady and predictable manner. India, therefore, did not come as a complete surprise. Rather, it was the realization of a desire that Middleton had already begun to express, and that the princess agreed to undertake such a demanding trip shows she felt ready to take the next step.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in India

Before the trip, Kensington Palace issued a statement emphasizing how much the princess cares about her husband’s environmental initiative and how meaningful it was for her to return to participate in the ceremony in person. “She’s enormously proud of what he’s achieved, and it has been particularly special for them to experience this moment together. They are very much a team.”

This refers to the project’s growth; since her last participation in Boston in 2022, it has significantly expanded its international reach and the impact of the initiatives it supports. “This year’s program in Mumbai promises to be the biggest and most ambitious yet, and she’s excited to see first-hand just how far some of it has come and meet some of the extraordinary people behind that success.” The spokesperson then recalled the couple’s previous trip to India in 2016, explaining that both have particularly fond memories of that visit. “The prince and princess are both really looking forward to what promises to be a fantastic week in India. They have such fond memories of their last visit together in 2016, and are excited to be returning a decade later.”

As mentioned, the most important diplomatic event of the tour took place on November 18 in New Delhi, where Prince William and Kate met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This was the only occasion during the visit when the royal couple left Mumbai, the city that hosted most of their scheduled engagements. Modi returned to the Indian capital specifically for this occasion after attending a major international summit in Manila, Philippines, to take part in the bilateral talks.

A spokesperson for Kensington Palace had emphasized the strategic importance of relations between the two countries, characterized by deep and ever-growing ties in numerous sectors, which include trade, investment, defense, security, technology, education, and culture. Kate’s presence alongside William during the meeting was considered particularly significant. “This meeting reflects the importance of that relationship, as well as the role their royal highnesses can play in celebrating and strengthening the ties between our two countries.”

“For the prince, it also represents another significant engagement as he continues to take on a growing role on the international stage. We’ve seen him increasingly support the UK’s diplomatic relationships through his overseas engagements, and this meeting will provide an opportunity to build on those connections at the highest level.”

India, after all, holds a special place in the history of relations between the British monarchy and the Commonwealth. King Charles has visited the country numerous times, on both official and private occasions, strengthening a personal and institutional relationship over the years. For William and Catherine, however, this trip represented an opportunity to build a direct relationship with a nation destined to play an increasingly important role in the international balance of power.

A close-up of the Prince and Princess of Wales

With a population of over 1.4 billion people, India is now the world’s most populous country and one of the fastest-growing economies. Hosting the Earthshot Prize meant engaging a potentially massive audience on issues of environmental sustainability, resource conservation, and innovative solutions to combat climate change.

A beautiful image of the Prince and Princess of Wales

For William and Kate, returning to India also meant revisiting a country to which they are bound by personal memories. As mentioned, their last visit was in April 2016, when the Prince and Princess of Wales—then the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge—undertook an official tour of India and Bhutan at the request of the British government. During that trip, they visited Mumbai, met with representatives from India’s cultural and sports communities, and traveled to Agra, where they admired the Taj Mahal.

Right in front of the famous mausoleum—a symbol of eternal love—William and Kate sat on the same white marble bench where, 24 years earlier, Lady Diana, Princess of Wales, posed during a visit to India. That photograph of Diana, portrayed alone in front of the monument, became one of the most iconic images of her public life. Taken in 1992, when her marriage to Charles was going through a deep crisis, many interpreted it as a visual representation of her loneliness. In 2016, William and Kate’s decision to recreate that shot inevitably brought Diana to mind, adding a personal and symbolic dimension to their visit.

For Catherine, therefore, this trip is above all a new step on her journey back to public life following her illness. Not a demonstration of recovery to be celebrated as a race against time, but an opportunity to resume playing an important role while moving at her own pace. And to stand once again alongside William on a mission that concerns not only the future of the monarchy, but also that of the planet.

Originally published by Vanity Fair Italy.

#3662. Don't expect a GTA set outside the USA anytime soon, as Rockstar has "not had a lot of conversations over doing it anywhere else"

"There never ceases to be a more interesting place."

Would Rockstar really set a future Grand Theft Auto game outside of the United States? The concept's been mooted recently, particularly in reporting on a recent Rockstar interview with The Guardian, where co-studio head Rob Nelson quipped: "Never say never." But speaking to Eurogamer in another interview since then, I would say it's unlikely.

During our conversation, I asked Nelson about the choice of the US as an ongoing setting for the games, and what in particular drove Rockstar's continuing infatuation with the country across both GTA and Red Dead Redemption.

"I don't know," Nelson said initially. "It's just that there never ceases to be a more interesting place to think about setting it. I just think that it's constantly changing, there's constantly stuff for us to respond to, and it works from a gameplay standpoint in terms of what we want to do."

A little more conclusively, he added: "We have not had a lot of conversations over doing it anywhere else."

That doesn't quite settle it for good, of course. Nelson's "never say never" comments still stand, but coupled with his follow-up response to The Guardian, where he noted "there's still so much to do in America," it seems we can pretty confidently pin the next GTA's location as somewhere, once again, within the United States.

I also wouldn't be surprised if there were early ideas as to where exactly within the US the next GTA might end up. The decision on Florida was one of the earliest Rockstar made this time, for instance. As Nelson explained to me, with GTA 6: "You first decide on place, for GTA – where are we going to set it?"

That was "quick", this time, he noted. "We had three major cities established, this was the one that we hadn't been back to recently. It's also felt [amongst the team]: if you want to reflect something about contemporary America, Florida is a pretty good place to give you a wide range of craziness, and sort of variety in terms of experience."

That then led to early research trips to Florida, Nelson explained, which in turn informed the game's characters and mechanics – including the more interactive, thoughtful, empathetic world Nelson also explained to me, and the decision around the big character moment in the early minutes of the game's prologue.

For much more on GTA 6's setting, meanwhile, our full GTA 6 map and extensive GTA 6 walkthrough might come in handy. And all this said, frankly, I'm more than happy to stay here in Leonida for some time - as was probably made quite clear in our five-star GTA 6 review.

If you’re wondering what Tucker Carlson thinks of breakout SNL star Jeremy Culhane’s buzzy impression, the unfortunate truth is we may never know. The popular talking head has apparently never seen it, and it’s not because he’s angry about it or opposed on principle, it’s because he’s against consuming any articles or videos about himself.

Fans love to joke about celebrities setting Google alerts for themselves, but if Carlson is to be believed, he tries to avoid any opinions about himself that don’t come directly from people he knows. He’ll listen to his family. He’ll listen to his friends and those working on his show. He wants their feedback, but when it comes to everyone else, he’d rather just tune out all the noise. Here’s what he told Brandon Straka during their interview...

I don’t watch anything or read anything about myself ever. That is my rule… Focusing on yourself too much is the road to unhappiness.

If that quote did something to you, it’s probably because Tucker uses one of the Tucker-isms Culhane uses all the time in his impression. It feels like every SNL appearance includes at least a couple usages of, “That’s the rule.” It warmed my heart to see it here, and it made me even more impressed with Culhane’s impression, given it almost felt in character the way Carlson said it. Seriously, first check out the interview with Carlson in real life…

I love how Straka basically has a panic attack the second he says, “That’s my rule.” In that moment, he’s all of us freaking out because he just said the thing. If you listen closely to the rest of Tucker’s comments, however, you can hear a lot more of where Culhane’s impression comes from. There’s the cadence in how he speaks, and of course there’s the signature laugh that Carlson has been known for throughout his career.

After his initial comments about never having seen the impression, Carlson went on to talk more generally about being parodied, and he had some really thoughtful things to say about his place in the world and what it’s like to get older. He said when he was a kid, he would look at older people and wonder if they were doing a bit, but as he’s aged and gotten feedback from his kids, he’s slowly realized that everyone sort of becomes a caricature of themselves.

He said he tries not to wear a mask, but sometimes he wonders if everyone eventually grows into one of the facets of their personality. Here’s a portion of his quote…

I do think we all become parodies of ourselves. I remember thinking that of older people when I was younger. I was like, ‘Are you serious? Are you acting? Is this like a bit?’ Maybe it was a bit 30 years ago, but now it’s who you actually are. Your face sorta grew into the mask you wore.

It sounds like Carlson is never going to watch Culhane’s impression, but I would love to see a reaction video of him checking it out for the first time, especially since he has more free reign outside Fox News. I wonder what would be going through his head, especially since it feels like a slightly exaggerated but also pretty realistic take on him as a talking head. It's hard to tell because celebrities have a wide range of opinions about getting parodied on the show. Elon Musk, as an example, doesn't like Culhane's take on him.

Regardless, I’m sure we’ll see Culhane’s impression quite a few more times on Saturday Night Live. It’s become a semi-consistent part of Weekend Update, and it gets tremendous feedback every time. Maybe we’ll even see it return when the show comes back with guest host Amanda Seyfried next weekend.

#3658. Rumored The Simpsons: Hit & Run remake may be in trouble after one developer says their "mind-blowingly awesome" project is cancelled

A rumored remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run (the internet's most-wanted video game revival) may be in trouble.

Just earlier this year, Radical Entertainment made somewhat of a comeback as New Radical Games - with the original studio's co-founder (Ian Wilkinson) and former developer (Tim Bennison) serving as New Radical's CEO and COO, respectively. The company best known for Prototype and the well-remembered open-world Simpsons game was back, in some sense.

Whatever project the studio was cooking hasn't been so lucky, it seems. New Radical Games senior game designer Darren Evenson recently said an upcoming project at the company had been scrapped, and he's now looking for new work, per a LinkedIn post.

"It seems that not even a fantastic project with an absolutely incredible team is immune from the current state of the industry right now, as what we were working on at New Radical Games (although mind-blowingly awesome) was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations," Evenson wrote. "A gaggle, I say!"

"Oh, you silly suits with spreadsheets... will you EVER learn? If you don't make the game, you can't make the money... and if you don't make the money, then you don't get the power... and... well, there's more to that quote, but I digress."

"For the first time in my career, I am Available For Work and looking for a new exciting opportunity where I can make some fun games with some great people," he added. "Please reach out, shout out, or perform some interpretive dance if you know of an opportunity that a hip cat like me could groove to."

New Radical Games has never formally revealed its plans, but a couple clues pointed to something Simpsons-shaped. As VGC noted, Evenson's statement echoes a few popular lines from the iconic animated sitcom. "Will you ever learn" is suspiciously close to a particular Troy McClure quote, for one.

Then there's seemingly a Scarface riff in the developer's statement - one that was also parodied in The Simpsons, of course: "In America, first you get the sugar, then you get the power, then you get the women." It's worth noting Radical Entertainment did also make Scarface: The World Is Yours, so this one could go either way.

But the most eyebrow-raising clue came from original Simpsons co-showrunner and creator Matt Groening. During a Disney D23 panel this summer, Groening and current showrunner Matt Selman were asked about the possibility of a Hit & Run comeback.

"I don't know [if] I'm speaking out of turn, I think the original game is coming back in some form," Groening said at the time, before Selman quickly chimed in: "Or not…"

"Hit & Run is so interesting. I'm a thousand years old, and when I was in my mid to late 20s, I helped write Hit & Run," Selman said back in March. "I had no idea it would become a cult game, a cult success. Of all the games, the thousands of Simpsons games... that one..."

#3657. Union Vote Fails In Landslide At GTA 6 Studio Rockstar Games As 75 Percent Of Devs Vote No

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6Rockstar GamesUnion

Rockstar Games will not be forced to formally recognize a union at the Grand Theft Auto 6 studio after its developers based in the UK voted overwhelmingly against the initiative. The weeks-long voting process played out as Rockstar launched the open-world hit to over 30 million sales in its first day.

Voting began on November 12 and concluded today on November 26. Workers at Rockstar Games voted 75 percent against the recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. The initiate would have formalized collective bargaining efforts around things like overtime, bonuses, layoffs, and AI. Developers in favor of unionizing can still work with the IGWB, but there will be no regular meetings with management to hash out new policies.

“We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe said in a statement shared with Kotaku. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.â

The IWGB Game Workers Union pushing the vote released the following statement:

For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isnât a sign to retreat, itâs a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. Weâre ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

Whilst we havenât emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But itâs one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. Weâll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.

The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.

The vote comes roughly a year after Rockstar fired dozens of developers it accused of gross misconduct and breaking confidentiality rules around the development of GTA 6. The fired workers accused the studio of union busting, which it has denied, and a legal fight has been ongoing over the last 12 months at a labor tribunal. A final judgement in that case is still pending. As recently as this month, members of both sides of the dispute were testifying on the record for the case.

#3656. Christmas in July? Why Stop There?

Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

Consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a New Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

If the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

So we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in New York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

But why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

Let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing important happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in New York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

And finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a big turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. But start figuring out your Valentine’s Day dates now—those prix fixe dinners with chocolate lava cakes really book up fast these days.

#3655. Yooka-Laylee studio explains upcoming Definitive Edition's absence on Xbox to 'frustrated' fans

"As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face."

Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is notably skipping Xbox Series X/S consoles, and the studio blames "technical challenges and costs."

The Definitive Edition is bringing support for 120fps, revamping the platformer's lighting, updating textures and shadows, and packaging in the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack DLC next month. But a large question mark hung over the lack of an Xbox version.

"Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th," developer Playtonic Games said in a new social media post.

"We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision. Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure… Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," it continued.

Playtonic said it understood Xbox players' frustrations, but the development costs associated with bringing the game to more platforms "just isn't viable for us at this time." Playtonic is still an independent game studio, after all, and Xbox console sales have been lagging behind the competition for quite a while.

"As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this. We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback," the statement went on.

Digital Foundry's John Linneman chimed in to tell folks that the omissions isn't a huge deal, because Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair already looks pretty great on Xbox consoles. "The Xbox One X version of this game is already native 4K," he tweeted. "The upgrade seems minor, thus it's already excellent on Xbox. Was the best console version by far."

The original Yooka-Laylee was a collectathon throwback in the same vein as Banjo-Kazooie, but this follow-up took more inspiration from Rare's Donkey Kong Country games instead - and the results were pretty stunning.

"It's the new in Impossible Lair which impresses, the tightness of the game's 2D controls and intricately designed levels which stands out, and which seems better fitted to Playtonic's toolbox," Eurogamer's review said. "It's a far more polished game than the studio's predecessor, and one well worth exploring through."

#3654. Lesley Manville, Pierce Brosnan, and More Celebrate Violinist Joshua Bell at the Langham London

At the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since. “I don’t remember falling in love with music,” says Bell. “Music has just been my life. I used to string rubber bands on my dresser drawers and make pitches by pulling the drawers out. I was fascinated with strings. It’s the closest instrument to the human voice. And I find it the most expressive instrument.”

Today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era. By 14, Bell was performing with the Philadelphia Orchestra, and would soon be touring the world. “I live in hotels 250 days a year,” says Bell of the nonstop schedule he has maintained since his teens. Specifically, Bell has been “staying at the Langham for decades now,” he says, referring to the regal central London hotel that first opened in 1865. “I chose it on my own because it was near one of my favorite halls in London, which is the Wigmore Hall. And now I stay with them whenever I’m traveling.”

That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.

Attendees included actor Simon Callow, House of Dragon actor Emily Carey, former British culture minister Ed Vaizey, Saturday Night Live UK cast producer Susie Hall, stage and television actor Indira Varma, and Verity actor Ismael Cruz Córdova.

Held in partnership with Vanity Fair, the evening marked the latest iteration of the Langham’s Luminaries in Residence program. The event series is continuation of the hotel’s legacy that brings together a diverse, influential community—an evocative reminder of prominent guests from its storied past, including Charles Dickens, Winston Churchill, George Orwell, Oscar Wilde, and Mark Twain.

“I’m not going to put my name in the same sentence as Toscanini or Mark Twain—who has stayed here, or Churchill, who has stayed here. But it’s cool to be part of the history,” says Bell. “So maybe someday, in a hundred years, there will be a violinist who might say that—that I stayed here. I don’t know, maybe that would mean something.”

It certainly does mean something. Pierce Brosnan and his wife, Keely Shaye Brosnan, “have been huge fans of Joshua for many, many years,” Brosnan tells me. “Keely went to go see him…I don’t know how many years back. Unfortunately, due to the LA traffic, she got there late, five minutes late, and they wouldn’t let her into the concert. So tonight is one of those nights.”

Bell, who performed mid-dinner with members of the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields—with a surprise appearance from his wife, soprano Larisa Martínez—brought about a collective catharsis.

Dazzling, fiery, and flamboyant, the experience of watching Bell up close is impossible to replicate. “I just think he’s incredibly soulful, and there’s something really elegant,” actor Russell Tovey tells me, before explaining how he actually discovered Bell via his Instagram algorithm.

For actor Lesley Manville, the event marked her introduction to Bell’s music. “I’m a bit embarrassed that he was not on my radar. But isn’t that nice to have a surprise like that?” says Manville. “Schubert’s String Quintet is one of my favorite pieces of music. It’s unbelievably beautiful. You think of a violin, you think of those strings. And it’s instant emotion. They just make you cry.”

There is a great power in being able to access the emotions of others, as Bell does.

“I think it is the ultimate gift to be able to make people happy,” says Brosnan. “My job is being an entertainer—to take the words of great writing and try to transform it into something that is meaningful and memorable.”

Speaking of entertaining, the week’s announcement that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond was front of mind. “I wish him every joy and every success. He and I made a movie a number of years ago called Remember Me. I played his father. So I was very, very pleased and joyful for his nomination and now his success, and I believe he will be magnificent.”

And that creative full circle is exactly what the night was advocating. “Our own Luminaries in Residence program reflects our belief that meaningful hospitality creates genuine connection with extraordinary talents with one another, and with arts,” Bob van den Oord, CEO of Langham Hospitality Group, explained as he took the stage. “The Langham isn’t simply a place to stay, but a place to gather, exchange ideas, and indeed celebrate.”

#3653. After drawing ire for selling new Mass Effect merch following BioWare closure, EA is now flogging new Dragon Age tat too

Seemingly unperturbed by the criticism it faced after selling new Mass Effect merchandise following the shock closure of developer BioWare, EA is now flogging new merchandise for the studio's other big series, Dragon Age.

EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel the long-awaited Mass Effect 5 in October was met with shock and condemnation from fans and games industry veterans alike. Legendary designer Warren Spector slammed the closure, and fan efforts to save the studio - including calls of support from Mass Effect voice acting talent - have continued in the aftermath.

EA, apparently aware of the potentially poor optics, quickly scrubbed a number of Mass Effect-themed cosmetics from Battlefield, but eyebrows were raised when, just weeks later, new Mass Effect merchandise - including a $175 wearable LED helmet - was released onto its BioWare Gear store on 'N7' day, the annual celebration of BioWare's space series. Unsurprisingly, more criticism followed. As one fan put it at the time, "This is such a bad look".

And now here we are again. EA'S BioWare Gear store has sprung to life once more, this time (thanks IGN) to promote a new "Seven Swords of Nightmare" hoodie inspired by BioWare's Dragon Age: Inquisition.

"Unless you reopen BioWare, EA, then no money for you," one person wrote in a social media response indicative of the general sentiment from others. Some users also used the opportunity to share the #savemasseffect hashtag beneath the BioWare Gear post - a related community initiative has so far seen over 330,000 fans sign a petition to save the series.

The community has been energised by glimpses of what could have been following Mass Effect 5's cancellation. At one point, a flashy internal trailer appeared online, and award-winning composer Austin Wintory also shared music he'd pitched for the game. Elsewhere, content creators claiming to have seen a work-in-progress version of Mass Effect 5 have called it "incredible" and claimed it would have drawn lessons from The Witcher and Baldur's Gate 3.

BioWare's closure in October came as part of the first round of layoffs at EA since the publisher's $55bn acquisition by a consortium including Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, investment firm Silver Lake, and private equity company Affinity Partners earlier this year. The move resulted in the loss of 400 jobs, with layoffs occurring across multiple studios, including Apex Legends developer Respawn, The Sims studio Maxis, and EA Motive.

#3650. Digital Extremes says Warframe's imminent Tau update is practically big enough to be a sequel as it reveals new details, including dog walking

Warframe's latest devstream has just gone live, revealing more about the new Tau solar system players will be able to explore as part of December's "massive" new update, which arrives on 9th December. Additions include a two-hour long quest, new explorable areas, and even chill nighttime dog walking.

In a press pre-briefing ahead of the Devstream, Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford and community director Megan Everett discussed the scale of the Tau update, revealing just how much of an ambitious undertaking it's been for the team. "This is a huge update, it is massive," Ford said. "It is a second solar system ... Alone, by now, this would have been Warframe two. We're just going for it: we're building a new solar system brick-by-brick."

That begins with a "two-hours-ish" story quest, according to Ford, but there's plenty more besides. Tau brings a new navigation system, for instance, and will feature two playable regions at launch. The World-Seeder Oasis is one: full of environmental hazards, thanks to damaging terraforming efforts, and various missions to complete. Here, players can go bug-collecting for an NPC called Catulast. Doing so increases your standing with him, and provides new rewards.

Then there's the ringed city of Fornax. Unlike previous regions in Warframe, this features three hubs: the Lastbloom Lounge, Manifold 90-BF, and the Elder Rustgarden. All have their own playable missions, some brand-new and others returning from the original star system. This includes Spy, a returning mode that has players breaking into terminals while trying to remain undetected.

Spy hasn't been shown a lot of love for a while, and it seems like this new iteration will bring new custom puzzles for players to take on. Ford notes it'll include codes to memorise, passwords to figure out, plus gameplay and an aesthetic that alights with the new Fornax setting.

Steel Path - the optional, more difficult variant of regular missions - also returns in Tau, although the Accolite mini-bosses who would hunt you down in previous Steel Path missions will not be present. Instead, the Hokra brothers will take that role: giant sentient casino goons who look quite daunting.

We were also shown more of the Last Bloom Lounge. Here you'll be given bounties that'll always bounce you between the three Fornax hubs. So, if you take one bounty in the Lounge, you'll complete it while out on a mission, and end up in either Manifold or the Rustgarden (which is still being kept secret for now). That way you'll be naturally circling between the three locations.

However, rather than there being three separate syndicate reputations to grind out, one single syndicate connects them all: the Fornax Informer, a newspaper run by kids obsessed with breaking stories across the ringed city. Print lives! By progressing through the ranks with this syndicate, you'll unlock clues for detective work that reveal a special cinematic within the Lounge, though this too is being kept secret for now.

By completing bounties, you'll also gain access to Fornax's own progression system which provides still-mysterious buffs and other beneficial effects within Tau. There's also a card game in the Lounge, which you can either play against the house or with other players.

As for navigating between the hubs, each one has its own garage. The Tau update comes with a driving minigame: an on-rails opportunity to gather resources and fend off other drivers along the way. In the demo shown, we're brought from the Lounge to the Manifold, dodging barriers and blowing up other sentient vehicles in the process. There's also a "low stakes, no combat" way to navigate between the hubs. It's called Night Walk, a first-person dog walking mode where you can travel

#3649. 12 Best Video Game Stocking Stuffers Under $30 That People Actually Want

Ugh. It’s my least-favorite time of year: Black Friday season. I hate this overwhelming capitalist-ass shopping holiday for many reasons, but one of my more petty pet peeves is the big push for the blandest, most cringey “gamer”-themed gifts ever at mainstream shopping destinations. I’m talking like, this “Smells like video game rage” candle, neon lights and blankets that say stuff like, “Can’t hear you, I’m gaming,” or the classic “I paused my game to be here” T-shirt. Crap that really leans into the awful “gamer” stereotype and that, for many of us, is embarrassing to receive from a relative who knows, like, one fact about us, which is that we are into video games.

If you’ve arrived at this article and have been guilty of giving such gifts before, please absolve yourself. The internet does not make this easy. Gaming gift guides are full of this junk, and if you’re not into games yourself, finding decent stuff for someone who likes them can be really annoying and challenging, especially on a budget. Most gamers probably have a lot of the tech and games they want already, and knowing what people have and what they might like can be extremely challenging if you don’t have an easy way to look at their Steam libraries.

So I’m here to give you a hand with 12 ideas for stocking stuffer gifts (read: will reasonably fit in a normal-sized Christmas stocking) under $30 that will probably be relevant to folks who like playing video games on the regular. These are all things that most people will be at least mildly pleased to receive and will probably use as long as you put in the bare minimum amount of thought to make sure you’re not getting Switch accessories for someone who doesn’t have a Switch or something.

Good controllers are so dang expensive and cheap ones are usually garbage, but the 8BitDo controllers are both of solid quality and inexpensive. These pleasant wireless controllers come in several cute pastel colors, are usable for PC gaming (or Android, I guess), and are quite inexpensive for as good as they are. Normally $29.99 on Amazon, as I write this they’re on sale for $22.99.

If you’ve got an Xbox gamer in the house, this charging stand works with all Xbox Series, One, and Elite Series 1 Wireless controllers, which your giftee almost certainly has at least one of. It’s normally $49.99, but Amazon has a Black Friday deal going that brings it all the way down to $18.99, so you may want to jump on it soon.

The Nintendo Switch 2 came out a year and a half ago, and with it came what’s effectively webcam support. However, my experience is that not a lot of people are using this feature, not because it’s a bad idea necessarily, but because they don’t want to buy the expensive bespoke webcam Nintendo is selling and don’t want to move the normal one they have on their PC over to their Switch every time. So right now, for $24.98 on Amazon ($34.99 normally) you can grab a Hori USB camera that’s licensed by Nintendo and works with the Switch 2. Actually having this set up with the Switch 2 will probably prompt more people to actually bust it out (it would certainly work on me).

If your gamer likes to sit at a desk, grab ’em a mug warmer like this Sweetfull option that’s currently $16.99, down from $19.99. It’s exactly what it sounds like, keeping the liquid warm. Great for tea, coffee, and hot cocoa drinkers who have told their families to stop buying them tea/coffee/cocoa every year because they now have too much.

It’s a little cliche, but I don’t know anyone who doesn’t think a light bar is at least a little cool. This one is inexpensive ($11.99 right now, down from $14.99), simple, and looks nice, though it’ll probably stick out of the top of the stocking a bit and give away your game.

Great for PC gamers. Comes in several colors and is $8 max when not on sale. Sounds lame, but is actually very useful. The sort of thing no one buys for themselves but is always grateful to get.

Check first, but an awful lot of people who are into video games pair that interest with a card-collecting hobby. PokÃ©mon cards are a nightmare to get nowadays, but if you can snag a pack or two from the 30th Celebration set, most PokÃ©mon card fans will be happy. Magic: The Gathering‘s Reality Fracture set is a good, safe bet for Magic fans, and the One Piece TCG is currently on a set called The Dominance of God.

Zojirushi is a great brand that makes a lot of great things, including water bottles. These are usually more expensive, but for Black Friday this blue one is down to $23.49 (other colors are also on sale under $30; I cover mine with stickers which you can do to give yours a personal touch). These things are durable and can support hot or cold bevvies, and from personal experience I can say it keeps cold water cold for hours. It’s easy to forget to drink water while engrossed in a really good game, and this bottle serves as a good reminder.

There are aÂ tonÂ of really cool, low-cost stickers, skins, and cases out there with which to protect one’s Nintendo Switch, and chances are your gamer wants one, because unless they have a sick special-edition Switch, those things are very bland aesthetically. Loads of them are under $30 and they come in all sorts of colors and styles. Just make sure you’re confident in which Switch (original or Switch 2) they have, so you get them one that fits.

This is another one of those items that I’d never go out of my way to buy for myself, but which I’d be grateful to receive and would absolutely give a whirl. Again, check and make sure you’re getting grips for the correct controller first: these work on Xbox or PlayStation.

Seriously. I don’t recommend gift cards as a singular gift for someone you care deeply about unless they ask for it explicitly, as it can come off as a bit thoughtless. But as one of several small items in a stocking for a younger relative or fellow adult you’re close to, this is a great additive option. A Steam gift card will go over well with almost anyone who plays games on their PC because they can buy whatever game has been on their wishlist without you having to guess at it. V-bucks are a great option if you know the person plays Fortnite. You can also get cards for the digital storefronts on PlayStation,Â Xbox, or Nintendo consoles. All of these will be welcome for anyone who uses these services.

#3647. Marvel's Iron Man might be planning to rear its head at The Game Awards, if EA Motive's updated website is any indication

EA Motive's Iron Man game has been quietly cooking away for a few years now, but don't worry. The wait to finally, officially see the superhero romp in action might be over soon, at least if the developer's updated website - two weeks before The Game Awards, no less - is any indication.

Redditors today noticed that EA Motive's official website got a little makeover recently. It's not clear when exactly the tweaks were pushed through, but the Wayback Machine makes clear that it's definitely been updated.

A new website look is by no means confirmation of an imminent announcement, of course, but there are a few other bits of evidence that certainly point in that direction.

For one, The Game Awards 2026 will air on Disney Plus for the very first time, alongside all the other platforms you're used to. "As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney's most anticipated titles in gaming," the film studio said earlier this month.

Kingdom Hearts 4, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra and more are definitely possible, too. Turmoil at Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Lyon makes that one a tricker guess, however.

Second is the fact that The Game Awards air on 10th December - eight days before the global opening of Avengers: Doomsday, a film that's shaping up to become the biggest cinematic event since the last time Marvel chucked all of its toys into the same sandbox and bashed them together. Giving one of the company's most popular superheroes the spotlight around the same time seems like a good idea.

This isn't the first time EA's Iron Man has popped up in recent times, either. What appeared to be an unfinished trailer for Motive's Iron Man leaked onto the internet this summer, and showed off blisteringly fast flying and lots of destructive gadgets. It looked further along than I expected, at least, so I wouldn't be surprised to see the billionaire playboy philanthropist rear his head again in two weeks time.

#3646. Are the Royals More Relatable Now Than Ever?

Prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power. Through their action-packed itinerary, which took them from Mumbai to New Delhi, the Prince and Princess of Wales have paved the way for a new style of royal tour.

From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

According to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret. “None of us knew she was presenting an award on the night, or that she was going to speak. The auditorium was packed. There were about 5,000 people there. It’s been the biggest Earthshot yet, and you could see Catherine was nervous, but she delivered an absolutely brilliant speech. I’d say her best yet.

“It’s been wonderful for her to be here, supporting William, and you can see they’ve really had fun. Because of ongoing terror threats, there have been less walkabouts, but it’s been a very successful and varied tour, and I think, being shorter than most tours, it sets a new blueprint when it comes to royal tours for the couple in the future.”

Prince William and Princess Kate arrive to attend the Earthshot Prize awards night at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

There are seemingly already plans for another royal tour, says Myers.

“William let slip that Australia is on the cards next, and if that’s the case, I imagine they will go as a family. They don’t want to be away from their children for too long, and what a way it would be to win support for the monarchy Down Under,” Myers says.

According to royals insiders, there had been some nervousness around the trip after the couple’s disastrous tour of the Caribbean in March 2022, when their visit was overshadowed by calls for the UK to apologize for slavery. Then some of their photo calls, including one that involved the couple riding in an open-top Land Rover, led to accusations of the royals appearing colonial and out of touch.

“I think there has been a slight nervousness about how this tour would be received, but the reception has been really good,” Myers says. “The fact that William and Catherine have included a visit to New Delhi to see Prime Minister Modi is a clever move. While this is a private trip to promote Earthshot, the Foreign Office was keen for William to meet with the Indian prime minister, so they have packed that into the itinerary too.”

The visit to India has come at a time when the royals are on something of a charm offensive following a difficult year for the royal family, from Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest to what one palace insider calls “the ongoing soap opera” with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has not been charged and has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.)

William and Kate are keen to carve out their own initiatives and projects focusing on their major priorities, including the environment, children’s early years, and mental health. With the challenge of having Harry and Meghan carrying out their own engagements, the Prince and Princess of Wales have been careful to establish clear parameters that set them apart as working royals. In one telling moment while on an engagement in Mumbai, Kate was asked for an autograph. She politely declined, so as not to breach protocol, a clear contrast to the Duchess of Sussex, who has signed autographs in the past.

“Catherine was asked to sign an autograph, but she was right not to. It wasn’t a snub; it was just adhering to protocol. An autograph could be sold for money,” notes Dickie Arbiter, former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II.

According to author Tom Bower, the royals are more relatable now than they were during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, who famously never gave a press interview. In recent weeks, Prince William has appeared as a guest on The Graham Norton Show (to promote Earthshot), and he’s revealed how he drinks his cider and his love of wild swimming as part of his guest-editing stint for a recent issue of Country Life magazine.

“The royals are more relatable, perhaps, than they ever have been, but they are not celebrities. There’s a danger of being too relatable, too much ‘one of the people,’ which means they can lose some of their mystery,” Bower says.

“William will have been advised to do TV appearances and take on media opportunities to bolster his public image. Of course, it’s charming to hear these nuggets and see this side of the prince, but I do think there’s a need to see and hear more from William about his broader plans. Over the years, Charles has made huge efforts to appeal to all cultural aspects of society. I’m not sure William has done that. He’s got to find a way of connecting with everyone, not just the younger generation,” Bower adds.

The Earthshot Prize awards have been a powerful way of demonstrating that William doesn’t just talk the talk; he is insisting on action.

“The Earthshot is a master class in what needs to be done,” concludes Arbiter. “He’s pushing for environmental issues and climate change, and he’s getting people to do something about it. The fact that he is so well supported, and by so many high-profile people, shows his pulling power and influence.”
