It's wild to think about but Survivor has been on the air for 26 years now. The competition series (which is streaming with a Paramount+ subscription) started its run back in 2000, and longtime fans are still up to date with the current Season 51. A lot has changed over the years, including Survivor's prize money, the amount of days the game lasts, and how casting works. I recently watched a vintage clip from back in Season 2, and it totally made me miss OG Jeff Probst.

The second season of the show was titled Australian Outback, and is arguably one of the best Survivor seasons in the show's long history. Some of the most iconic players ever came out of Season 2, including Jerri Manthey and the great Colby Donaldson. I recently saw a clip of a wildly dangerous challenge, and I was shook by how different the entire show feels nowadays. You can check out the video for yourself below:

A post shared by Susie Mac (@survivordeepdive)

Honestly, how crazy is this Survivor challenge? Rather than the standard ones we're used to seeing every season, the above clip shows Jeff asking the cast to jump off a cliff and try to survive floating down rapids with boxes of supplies. It's truly terrifying to watch it play out, especially when you consider that Rodger Bingham had only JUST learned to swim before starting the game.

I loved re-watching this unique challenge, as I've grown tired of seeing the same ones every single season. I mean, how many times can we watch the contestants do the same puzzle? The show's early seasons used to have challenges that were themed based on their location, making each one unique. Although as we know, Survivor has been permanently based in Fiji since Season 33. So the location-based theming has been gone since 2016.

Seeing this retro Survivor clip also made me miss the OG version of host Jeff Probst. While he's pretty warm and cuddly nowadays, he used to be more of a hard ass. I used to love hearing him throw shade at the contestants, often adding salt to fresh wounds in the process. Seriously, he used to call people or tribes "completely useless" back in the day. This always cracked me up, but nowadays the host/showrunner is more likely to give folks a warm hug.

Jeff used to be scary during classic Survivor, but that's simply not the vibe anymore. I mean, castaways are so comfortable around him they're willing to interrupt his speeches and even give him a nickname like "Uncle Jeff." Where's the respect, people?

Survivor airs new episodes Wednesdays as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see if Probst ends up changing his tune at all throughout the rest of Season 51.

#3567. I Tried Building My Own Interactive World in Google Genie, but Real-Time AI Engines Aren't There Yet

David Nield is a technology journalist from Manchester in the U.K. who has been writing about gadgets and apps for more than 20 years.

He has a bachelor's degree in English Literature from Durham University, where he also spent a term as editor of the award-winning student newspaper Palatinate. His journalism career started in print media, where he contributed to and edited several technology magazines and bookazines sold in the U.K. and internationally. More recently, he has worked as a freelancer for some of the biggest technology publications on the web, covering everything from on-the-ground reporting about product launches, to detailed explainers and how-to guides on apps, gadgets, and platforms. His expertise covers broad areas of consumer tech, including smartphones, laptops, wearables, and AI.

Beyond the Gemini assistant, Gemini Notebook, and various other AI offerings, Google also develops Genie, a world-building engine intended to help you create immersive visual experiences and games using only text prompts. Think of them like AI videos you can interact with and move through.

With the recently launched Genie 4 update, this tool is purportedly even more powerful. It now allows you to request live edits (like "make it snow") and incorporate sound and dialog into your prompts. Google is also promising more realistic physics and natural movements in its renderings.

These promises point to the future of AI in all kinds of ways—from robotics to world sims—but the tool requires a lot of computing power, and access is limited for the time being. You can dive in now if you're on one of the Google AI Ultra plans ($99.99 or $199.99 a month), or join the waitlist if you're a Google AI Pro user ($19.99 a month). But if you've got access, is it worth the effort (and money)? I put it to the test.

It's no exaggeration to say you can build an entire virtual world in Google Genie. It's going to be a more basic, less developed, and more chaotic world than the one in, say, GTA 6, but you can do it. Think of it like generating an AI video from a prompt, but you can then walk through the video and go as deep as you like, taking turns along the way.

Everything is rendered in real time, at a resolution of 720p and at 24 frames per second. That's not to say the engine is storing a massive 3D map in memory, however—after a minute or so, it's going to start to forget the places you've already seen. And while the basic layout will stay fixed, you might notice disappearing trees or changing colors.

Google's official line is "visual details and object permanence can still shift or drift over time" in Genie 4, so it's a known limitation. The tool is presented as-is, with the intention to develop it further over time as models improve, and it's aimed at filmmakers, historians, designers, scientists, robotics engineers, and game developers. Or indeed, anyone who just wants to get lost in a world that isn't real.

Some of the demos you'll find as you step through the Genie 4 portal give you a great idea of the possibilities. There's a "Dino Field Guide" that, you guessed it, lets you wander safari-style through a prehistoric habitat. All the flora and fauna are neatly rendered, and you even get dinosaur quiz questions along the way—a nod to Genie's potential as an educational tool.

There's a "Villa Giallo" mini-game, which involves searching a haunted 1970s Italian villa and clicking on objects as you go; these objects act as clues to help you progress to the next room. I was also intrigued by a "White House: Code Red" experience that takes you into the West Wing during a "high-stakes national crisis." I couldn't quite figure out what the crisis was, but I definitely felt the highness of the stakes.

Someone's even built a "GTA 7" engine that drops you into a bright and vibrant cityscape. The slow speed and warped physics of the experience suggest Rockstar Games has nothing to worry about just yet—check out the disappearing cars and backwards-driving cops in the video above—but it's impressively detailed all the same, considering it all comes from a few text prompts.

Having checked out a few demos, I felt ready to put Genie 4 to the test myself. Eager not to infringe on any IP, I decided to generate a world where I wouldn't mind getting lost for a few minutes—somewhere I could get away from the stress of my day and enjoy some warmer weather.

I started with the prompt "Create a fully immersive, photorealistic 3D environment showing a pub in an English village in the middle of a hot and sunny day. The pub is surrounded by country lanes, old buildings, and woods, and a handful of villagers are walking around and drinking outside the pub. Use a first-person view and use a quiet background of birdsong and wind rustling in the trees."

It took a couple of minutes for my peaceful, idyllic world to be ready, and then I was immediately able to navigate through it using my keyboard and mouse. Once you're in your world, you are suggested certain prompts you can make use of, like strolling into the pub or getting the villagers to make a toast, and these worked well—evidence that your virtual world really is interactive (to a point).

Unsurprisingly, the usual AI video tells are in abundance: Everyone looks generic, the physics often go sideways, the text on signs is gibberish, and details don't remain fixed. Do a full 360-degree spin around, and you might find that not only have all the customers in the pub changed their appearance, but you're also at an entirely different pub.

The best feature is the ability to make real-time edits: I summoned both a storm and a cricket pitch with a few text prompts, though Genie decided to put a hut in the middle of the cricket pitch for some reason. I think I was most impressed by the moment when a cricketer walked past me and commented on the rain, providing hints of how this kind of tech could expand or augment games and virtual experiences in the future.

That said, even at v4 of Genie, this tech is still very much in the experimental stage, and while I can see the potential, it also shows just how difficult a task world-building is for an AI engine. Without 3D maps and proper physics engines as a foundation, you'll encounter a great deal of hastily rendered slop as you explore your environment. Even if you're a prompting pro, for the time being this is something to mess around with, rather than use in a practical way.

#3566. Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Missions–It Felt “Alien And Disconnected”

One of the first things people noticed with Grand Theft Auto 6 is that you cannot replay missions, at least not in a simple, straightforward way. GTA 5 had a mission replay option, as did Red Dead Redemption II, so why doesn't GTA 6?

Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku that Rockstar "certainly" considered a mission replay feature "early on in development." However, Butchard said, "As the game came together, it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected."

He went on to say replaying missions "really diminished the choices you had made."

While GTA 6 doesn't make it easy to replay missions, you still can do so by reloading an earlier GTA 6 save. Something else to know is that if you're in the middle of a mission and it's not going to plan, you can open the game menu and select retry, quit, or restart.

GTA 6 blasted off with 32.5 million sales via prepurchases alone and around $4 billion in revenue on day one. The game is only going to get bigger and sell more copies over time, and it's helping drive new PlayStation and Xbox hardware sales.

In other GTA 6 news, the actor who plays the character Mandy has reacted to people being weird online. Rockstar has also reacted to the sentiment that GTA 6 is too easy.

#3565. Jordan Rodgers Calls Brother Aaron's Steelers Departure 'Sad to See'

Jordan Rodgers is admittedly shocked by his brother Aaron Rodgers’ departure from the Pittsburgh Steelers.

“That was something we weren’t all preparing for,” Jordan, 38, quipped on the Friday, November 27, broadcast of Good Morning America. “It was a crazy couple days for the Steelers and Aaron. I think that first and foremost, it’s just kind of sad to see it end this way in Pittsburgh.”

He continued, “There was so much good vibes and hope about the reuniting of [Mike] McCarthy and Rodgers and the potential to make a playoff run one last dance. Unfortunately, it didn’t happen that way.”

Aaron, 42, signed with the Steelers in 2025. The team benched him from Friday’s game, shortly before the quarterback claimed that head coach McCarthy, 63, was “unhealthy” in a bombshell interview. While McCarthy has refuted the claims, the Steelers have since parted ways with Aaron.

“I think what’s getting lost in this, though, is just how unacceptable and unprecedented some of the behavior that McCarthy has displayed and how unique that is,” Jordan added on Friday. “I think I would be surprised if he continued to be the head coach moving forward, whether that’s short-term, long-term, whatever it is. I think, having been in locker rooms … there’s too many jobs at stake for people to put up with that behavior.”

He speculated, “I think the Steelers will look into this, but seemingly, the accusations and allegations are confirmed in a lot of ways, and he didn’t refute them. Crazy world that we’re living in, but [it’s a] weird way to see it end.”

Jordan and Aaron recently reunited following a longtime estrangement. Jordan first revealed their family drama on a 2016 episode of his now-wife JoJo Fletcher’s season of The Bachelorette, which his brother later criticized for publicizing their family issues.

Aaron slowly started mending fences with his parents and brothers, Luke and Jordan, following his 2025 wedding to wife Brittani.

“There was some stuff there and then I could tell I was coming to a time where I needed to make it right,” Aaron said on a September episode of the “Not Just Football” podcast, detailing the “tough” conversations the now-reunited relatives had. “I’m in a much better headspace, and I said it before, but my wife deserves a lot of the credit for that just to be even able to to get to that point where I could think about having the conversation.”

#3564. Another Live-Service Game Is Going Extinct, And This One Has Dinosaurs

Capcom has had a big year, but amid the hits comes news that its Overwatch-with-dinosaurs game, Exoprimal, will join the live-service graveyard next year. The game's servers will go offline next year, making it unplayable after that.

"Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal, a statement on the Exoprimal site reads. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of Thursday, September 30, 2027. We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement."

Exoprimal season passes are no longer available to purchase through storefronts, and Capcom will slowly wind down the game over several months. Exoprimal and all its DLC will be delisted from stores starting March 30, 2027, but anyone who owns it can still download and play it before the September 2027 deadline. Despite a cool premise and fun gameplay, Exoprimal never truly took off after its 2023 launch.

"While Exoprimal’s early hours of repetitive and simple missions will likely drive some people away, its later surprises are a delight for those willing to give it the necessary time," James Carr wrote in GameSpot's Exoprimal review. "The escalation of difficulty and the wide variety of objectives introduced later on in the shooter gives it fresh life several hours in. Fighting through an ocean of dinosaurs is a ton of fun, and the variety of enemies keeps you from falling into a repetitive combat loop."

The writing was already on the wall for Exoprimal in 2024, as Capcom announced it was ending seasonal updates and would rotate through existing content on a monthly schedule. While that doesn't reflect the entire player community, Exoprimal numbers have largely cratered on PC via Steam: it peaked at 4,9995 concurrent players in November 2023 and nosedived the following month. At the time of writing, Exoprimal's 24-hour peak was a paltry 23 players.

2026 has been merciless for live-service games, with several high-profile casualties. Developer Wildlight’s free-to-play shooter Highguard quickly lost momentum after its January launch, Anthem was sunset this year, and New World: Aeternum began winding down operations ahead of its January 2027 closure.

#3563. Tidal Is the First Streaming Platform to Ban AI Music

You have a few options when it comes to choosing a music streaming service. If you own an iPhone and a Mac, you might be tempted by Apple Music; if you have more friends on Spotify, you may feel that's the best platform for you. But if your goal is avoiding AI music as much as humanly possible, there appears to be a new uncontested winner: Tidal.

On Tuesday, Tidal announced plans to ban AI music from its platform entirely. Starting Dec. 9, the company will begin taking steps to remove music it believes is entirely made with AI. Tidal says it thinks the move “will resonate with both artists and listeners alike.”

This isn't the first stand Tidal has taken against AI-generated music. Back in July, the company announced that it would start labeling songs completely made with AI, as well as remove tracks it found to be "fraudulent and deceptive." Other platforms have similar policies, or are rolling out similar features. Apple Music, for example, is working on AI labels for its app, too, and Spotify has pushed back on AI to some degree. However, this most recent move makes Tidal the first music streaming service to outright ban AI-generated music from its catalog.

Robert Anderson, Tidal's Music Lead, posted on X about the change. According to Anderson, Tidal identified 43% of the tracks it received in the last 90 days were AI-generated. Per the company's plan, Tidal will remove 29 million songs by the beginning of 2027, roughly 80,000 to 85,000 removals per day. Some 96% of Tidal's AI-generated songs have zero plays whatsoever.

I wouldn't be surprised to see other music streaming services follow suit, particularly Apple Music. Despite rolling out AI-powered features over the past couple of years, including Apple Music's AI-generated playlists, Apple has taken some stands against AI-generated material in general. The latest Apple TV intro was shot in-camera with practical effects, in an era where the company could have easily generated something with AI. If other companies plan to follow Tidal's lead here, my money's on Apple being first in line.

However, as it stands, Tidal is the only streaming service that supports this initiative. Soon enough, it'll be the sole music app you can use with near-zero ambiguity that the music you're listening to was at least mostly created by humans. (What a sentence.) Avoiding AI-generated music can be tricky, frustrating, and, frankly, exhausting. If that's important to you, Tidal might just be your new pick.

#3562. Prince William Reportedly Wants to Strip Prince Harry of His Titles

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”

The plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”

By implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”

#3561. Diablo 4’s Most Nostalgic Season Is Becoming (Mostly) Permanent

Diablo 4 is gearing up for the arrival of Season 16, but it won't be leaving its popular previous season behind entirely.

As detailed by Blizzard in a breakdown of the upcoming Season of Tyrael's Gambit, much of the previous season, Hell's Legacy, will become a permanent part of Diablo 4 going forward. Season 15 served as celebration of the franchise's history, and added a smorgasbord of items and callbacks to previous Diablo titles, including a storyline revolving around Deckard Cain and the return of enemies and boss encounters from Diablo 2. 

Most of that is carrying forward, Blizzard said. Due to "overwhelming requests" from the game's community, Blizzard outlined what all from Hell's Legacy will survive.

Hell's Legacy's capstone dungeons will be added, as will the ability to summon a World Boss version of Diablo and take on the cow god Moopisto. The Prime Evil Council is also becoming permanent, and will work the same way the game's other Lair bosses do, with players needing a specific item to open their reward chest after successfully defeating the encounter.

Waking Nightmare dungeons will still be accessible, but only by finding Chronicle of Nightmares dungeon keys. Monsters from previous Diablo games will also have a chance to spawn in The Pit. Those who progressed their secret cow level journey can also rejoice, as the secret cow island and its corresponding waypoint will be staying.

Many of Hell's Legacy's best items were new versions of classics from older Diablo games, and those Legacy Uniques will be added permanently as well, including the Annihilus Seal and Hellfire Torch Charm.

That's all for now, but Blizzard said more of Hell's Legacy could make a return in the future.

"Other popularly requested features are being evaluated for rework and may appear in the future," Blizzard said.

Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. In addition to bringing forward much of Hell's Legacy, Tyrael's Gambit will additionally overhaul the game's War Plans system and make its Helltide activity easier.

Diablo 4 won't receive new expansions going forward, but it is receiving a new class, the Amazon, next year. Blizzard is also hard at work on Diablo 5. Though it's not slated to arrive until 2029, Blizzard has already revealed three of Diablo 5's playable classes and promised it will launch with more class options than any previous Diablo game.

She continued: “I was expecting to get booted out. I really was. I don’t know why. You know when you have that gut feeling? But then I say this, but my gut is never right. Like, look at me in The Traitors, so I don’t know why I listen to it.”

Higgins’ time on DWTS came with its fair share of highs and lows.

“This week was definitely one of the toughest I’ve had so far,” Higgins wrote via Instagram following Disney Night. “I was really unwell, running on very little energy and trying to learn two dances, but I gave it absolutely everything I had❤️.”

She offered a glimpse into what challenged her, adding, “I came into this experience knowing I wasn’t a dancer, a performer or an athlete, but I wanted to challenge myself, step outside my comfort zone and give something completely new my absolute best & that’s exactly what I’m trying to do every single week.”

Higgins noted that she is still “learning” when it comes to performing.

“I’m making mistakes, I’m pushing myself and I’m growing along the way!!” she continued. “Some weeks will be better than others, and that’s okay. I’m only human🥹.”

She concluded: “I’m not sharing this for sympathy or to make excuses, but simply to share a little of the reality behind the scenes! Sometimes all you can do is show up, give everything you have and be proud of yourself for trying!! A special thank you to my incredible partner @markballas who has been my biggest support throughout this journey. His patience, encouragement and belief in me, especially during such a difficult week, mean more than he knows. I genuinely couldn’t have asked for a better person to share this experience with❤️.”

Higgins famously received an Hermès Birkin bag of her own from Traitors costar Rob Rausch after he blindsided her to win season 4 earlier this year.

#3559. I Love Hallmark Christmas Movies, And There Are Two Great Ones You Can Only Watch Streaming

As Christmas inches closer, fans are getting more into the spirit thanks to the 2026 Christmas movie schedule. Hallmark once again offers a large variety of classics and has over two dozen new holiday films this year. A massive number of people have already been watching Countdown to Christmas. However, the network’s beloved lineup does not just include the main channel. Hallmark’s Christmas classics have also made their way to Hallmark+. I love the holiday films, and there are two great ones that you can only watch on streaming, for the most part, that is.

Get in on this Black Friday deal through Amazon to save big on your first three months and watch all the best Christmas and other holiday movies the streamer has to offer. Including movies that are only available on Hallmark+.

Now that Thanksgiving is over, fans are looking forward to the holiday season. And to get into the Christmas spirit, if you haven’t already, Hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas is just the thing. Of course, while the network has been showing Christmas movies 24/7 for several weeks now, Hallmark+ has even more to watch. And that means even more movies that actors have had to film during the summer. For Black Friday, fans can sign up for just $2.99 for the first three months (perfect for those upcoming cold winter nights). That includes many Hallmark series and movies, as well as exclusive originals only available on Hallmark+. After those three months, it's either $8.99 per month or $79.99 per year, and it includes plenty of great offers.

As previously mentioned, there are a handful of originals exclusively for Hallmark+, such as the When Calls the Heart prequel Hope Valley: 1874, which is coming back for Season 2. This includes the four-movie Unwrapping Christmas collection that premiered back in November 2024. Even though they premiered two years ago, the movies definitely still hold up, and two of them are arguably the best in the series.

Unwrapping Christmas follows four friends working at a gift-wrapping shop leading up to the town’s Christmas gala. Similar to The Wedding Veil series, each movie centers on a different friend and their Christmas romance. The first one, Unwrapping Christmas: Tina’s Miracle, stars Natalie Hall as the titular Tina Mitchell, the owner of said gift-wrapping shop. She finds herself in a bind after the Christmas gala she’s planning is nearly canceled until she teams up with an estate company owner to save the venue.

Of course, Hallmark is no stranger to plots about saving a business or building in time for the holidays. And the network has been criticized for being too formulaic. That being said, Tina’s Miracle is still a great watch because it sets up the rest of the movies and her own love life. She’s hesitant to open up because of a past breakup, but ultimately, she and Michael (Alec Santos) team up to save the historic venue Alford House. With some twists and turns included, it’s perfect.

The second and third movies, Mia’s Prince with Kathryn Davis and Lily’s Destiny with Ashley Newbrough, are definitely fun watches and can get anyone into the spirit. However, I do love the fourth movie, Olivia’s Reunion, which sees gift-wrapping expert Olivia (Cindy Busby) getting snowed in with her ex while delivering gifts ahead of the gala. I am a sucker for a good enemies-to-lovers plot, especially if said enemies were previously together. Putting the characters in a closed space for an undisclosed amount of time, you never know what could happen. Plus, Jake Epstein, who plays the ex, has a soft spot in my heart after portraying Craig Manning on Degrassi: The Next Generation.

All four Unwrapping Christmas movies ultimately premiered on Hallmark Channel in July 2025, but seeing that they are Hallmark+ exclusives, I couldn’t help but relive them. Fans can relive those movies and plenty more Hallmark favorites on Hallmark+. Countdown to Christmas is far from over, and there is a movie for everyone.

#3558. Three Years After His Death, EA Is Using AI To Bring Back A Famed Commentator In FC 27

EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.

Motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005. According to the BBC, EA approached Motson's wife and son for permission to regenerate his voice and use his likeness for this year's entry in the series. Both agreed to the idea, but neither party has disclosed how much EA has paid for the use. Fred Motson, John's son, stated that he believed his father would've approved of this use of AI.

"My dad was the least technological person in the world," Fred stated. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically, but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects."

Peter Caulfield, founder of Save Our Voices Now, which campaigns against this exact use of AI, questions whether a family should be able to provide consent for someone who can no longer give it themselves. "If someone has signed a deal allowing their likeness to be used after they die, I have no issue with that," he explained. "But in life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed. Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either."

This isn't new to video games, either. Epic Games used a similar method to bring back the late James Earl Jones' voice for its Star Wars event in Fortnite, with the actor's estate agreeing to the use. It allowed players to converse with the AI bot while playing, and was very quickly removed after some users managed to get the bot to spew out racist or vulgar phrases, all delivered with the voice of Jones. It also drew the ire of SAG-AFTRA, which claimed that Epic had violated labor practices.

Derek Rae, one of the currently employed commentators on EA Sports FC 27, said he was excited by the inclusion of Motson's voice, and that he didn't believe AI was yet going to replace his own work on the game. When asked whether he would make the same decision to have his work endure for years to come through AI, he replied, "I'm hopefully many years away from having to make a decision like that."
